reader.requirement: The WRITE operand of the 1985 format is record-name-1 alone: it must name a logical (01-level) record of an FD in the File Section, qualified by its file-name where needed (OF/IN); the compiler must accept every such form on relative files (and the other organizations) and refuse a Working-Storage item, a subordinate item of a record, an SD record, an ambiguous unqualified name, a wrong qualifier, a reference-modified name, a file-name in its place, and the 2002+ WRITE FILE form.

edition-consulted.switches: WRITE FILE file-name-1 (construct write-rewrite-file-phrase-2002): refused COBOL0900 at 85, accepted at 2023; the record-name-1 arm itself is edition-free

reader.edition-search: ResolveWriteRecord, ResolveRecordName, FileWhoseRecordIs and KeyedIoBinder.BindWrite grepped for Edition.Edition|Year|CobolVersion: no comparison; the record identity test is the same code at every edition. The FILE alternative is gated through Constructs.WriteRewriteFilePhrase2002 (grep of the construct id).
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: 2002+ add the WRITE FILE file-name-1 alternative, which 85 refuses; the record-name-1 rule is identical

reader.notes: ResolveRecordName is asked before the sequential/keyed reroute, so a relative WRITE is under the same identity test. refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VIII.4.9.2 format and 4.9.3 SR1-SR2. Probes at 85: rwr2a - a contained program WRITEs records of the container's GLOBAL relative FD (GREC, and REC OF GRF where its own FD LRF also has an 01 REC) and its own REC unqualified: printed 'INNER ST=00 LST=00 / OUTER ST=00 / R1=[GGGG] / R2=[OOOO]' (scope of names resolves the local REC to LRF, the qualified one to GRF). rwr2b - a 66 RENAMES item, a level-88 condition-name and a Linkage record as record-name-1: each refused (COBOL1757, COBOL1639, COBOL2746+COBOL1757). rwr2c - a contained program WRITEs a record of a NON-global FD of its container: refused COBOL1639 not defined. rwr2d - EXTERNAL relative FD, record named in lowercase and qualified 'write XREC of xrf': printed 'ST=00 / R=[XXXX]'. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VIII.4.9.3 SR2  (4.9.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2'. Cosmetic: for the RENAMES item COBOL1757 says 'subordinate to REC' (a 66 is not subordinate); the refusal is right.
